trust_decision.summary: The StreamableHTTPTransport treats the caller-supplied Mcp-Session-Id header as proof of session ownership: handle_post, handle_get and handle_delete act on any session whose ID is presented, after only existence and idle-timeout checks, and no code anywhere compares the request's principal or Origin against the session that was created at initialize.

landing_point.why: An engineer reading only 'SSE session poisoning' looks at the POST dispatch first, and the notification branch is the weakest one: it is the only POST branch that dispatches into the session named by the header without even checking that the session exists (dispatch_notification at :647-658), so a foreign session ID writes into a victim's ServerSession state.

fix_sites.entry_point: POST / (Rack app call -> handle_request -> handle_post): non-initialize dispatch restructured, one gate covering notification, client-response and regular-request shapes
new private check validate_session_request(request, session_id) inserted next to extract_session_id
POST / initialize -> handle_initialization gains the request argument
POST / initialize -> @sessions record gains the :origin field
forbidden_response gains a default message (403 helper reused by the new gate)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: O2 and O8 are empty, so the only dismissal available is for the neighbour routes the fix does gate: a solver can argue GET only reads a stream and DELETE only ends a session, so only the POST tool-call path is 'session poisoning' - the published fix rejects that reading by gating GET and DELETE too.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Non-browser clients that send no Origin header (curl, scripts) must keep working, and stateless mode must stay untouched because it retains no sessions - an over-broad fix that requires an Origin, that treats a missing Origin as a mismatch, or that gates the initialize handshake or stateless POSTs, breaks both.

O6_input_shapes: regular request POST (body has id and method)
notification POST (body has method, no id) - e.g. notifications/cancelled
client response POST (body has id, no method)
GET that attaches the session's SSE stream
DELETE that tears the session down
Origin header equal to the one recorded at initialize
no Origin header at all (non-browser client)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A legacy query-string session lookup (?sessionId=) added to extract_session_id beside the header read.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The project's own example middleware already reads sessions from the query string (examples/streamable_http_server.rb:93), so a maintainer adding backward compatibility for pre-header clients is a natural, plausible change that would re-open the same sink without the gate.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A resumability/replay route (Last-Event-ID event store) that re-attaches or replays a session's buffered stream by session ID.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The file carries an explicit TODO saying resumability is not implemented yet, so a maintainer implementing it would add a new per-session read path that must be added to whatever ownership gate exists.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A public Server#handle_json(session_id:) front door that resolves a session itself, parallel to the transport's per-request ServerSession routing.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Server#handle_json is already public and both transports call it, so a maintainer exposing a session-scoped convenience API (or an adapter for another Rack framework) there is realistic and would bypass validate_session_request entirely.

O9_family: Improper access control: session identifier used as a bearer credential with no binding between session and caller (session hijacking / state poisoning across sessions)

O10_build.toolchain: Bundler + Rake; Ruby >= 2.7 (mcp.gemspec:17); runtime deps json_schemer, rack (required lazily by the transport); minitest + mocha + webmock + active_support for tests (Gemfile:27-33); rubocop optional
O10_build.project_tests: test/mcp/server/transports/streamable_http_transport_test.rb (~4800 lines, in-process Rack requests: session CRUD at :498-767, per-session client info and logging at :4226-4270, origin/DNS-rebinding at :4444-4698) plus test/mcp/server/transports/streamable_http_notification_integration_test.rb; run with `rake test` (Rakefile:6-11). The fix's new tests are not present at the pinned commit.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add one Origin-equality (or validator) check to the regular-request POST branch only, and require an Origin header, leaving the notification and client-response POSTs, GET and DELETE ungated and rejecting non-browser clients.

out_of_scope_notes: lib/mcp/client/http.rb:519-520 accepts whatever Mcp-Session-Id the server returns and keeps it for the connection lifetime (client-side session fixation surface) - outside this advisory's server-side protection, not pursued.
unverified: Full advisory text was not available (no network); the protected property and its documented exceptions are taken from the fix diff and the README section it adds (fix.diff:13-36).

repo_mb was not measurable (no shell). The tree has 156 files, the largest source file is ~1090 lines and the largest test file ~4900 lines, so tiny_repo (<5 MB of source) is inferred rather than measured.
No latest release was supplied for this entry ('none'), so present_in_latest is unknown for all routes.

Whether hidden tests demand the exact public API shape (kwarg name session_request_validator, 403 status, ->(request, session_id) arity) cannot be checked; if they do, the task reduces to matching the published interface rather than discovering scope.

Deliberately not recorded as O8: a non-initialize POST notification carrying an unknown or expired session ID still reaches the shared Server via dispatch_notification (lib/mcp/server/transports/streamable_http_transport.rb:647-658), and the published gate returns true when no session record exists; the advisory's property is scoped to existing sessions ('against an existing session', fix.diff:21-22), so this is a neighbouring sink, not an uncovered route into the same one.
`rake default` also runs conformance, which shells out to npx and is skipped when npx is absent (Rakefile:54-59); the transport tests themselves need no network.
